program.name: History & Social Studies (umbrella profile)
program.description: Academic humanities curriculum reconstructed from publicly documented LI courses; tests whether the analysis engine supports non-CTE academic programs.

source.title: After the Diploma public-source curriculum reconstruction v0.1
source.notes: NOT an official LI syllabus. Seven courses are publicly documented; specific competencies are labeled inferred or proposed where the source does not establish them. Faculty validation required before institutional use.
source.original_text: Lyndon Institute offers History and Social Studies coursework including Culture and Geography (rivers and civilization; geography and culture; currencies, trade routes and exports; tourism, food production, the space race; Alaska, colonization, economy and climate change; student-selected research topics), Genocide and Human Rights (historical and contemporary human rights cases including Anne Frank/Holocaust studies, Armenian genocide and Uyghurs), AP European History, AP U.S. History, Civics and Constitutional Law, Sociology, and Sophomore Humanities Honors. School-wide Portrait of a Graduate competencies include communication, self-direction, creative and practical problem-solving, collaboration, and community engagement.
